verdict_reasoning: The goal has support in the thread, and the LSN epoch answers the old blocker of catalog writes during recovery. Three design points are still open. replication-ondisk-1 shows a path where pg_upgrade can mark an empty unlogged matview as populated. standards-compat-1 shows that removing relispopulated breaks clients on clusters that never use the feature. standards-compat-2 is a pg_dump rule the thread left open.

brief.title: Unlogged materialized views with an epoch-based populated state
brief.problem: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW on large views is slow and writes a lot of WAL. The author targets users whose materialized views need not survive a crash, such as caches, rollups and lookup tables that can be rebuilt. Earlier threads agreed such views should become unpopulated after a crash, but pg_class cannot be updated during recovery.
brief.proposed_design: pg_class.relispopulated (bool) becomes relpopulated (int8): 0 is unpopulated, 1 is crash-safe populated, any other value is an epoch stamp for an unlogged matview. pg_control gains a durable LSN marking where WAL ended at the last unlogged reset. A stamp older than the current epoch reads as unpopulated, so crash, promotion and PITR invalidate the view with no catalog write during recovery.
user_visible_surface: create unlogged materialized view and alter materialized view ... set { logged | unlogged }.
pg_class.relispopulated removed and replaced by relpopulated int8, so queries that read relispopulated fail.
New function pg_matview_is_populated(regclass), which pg_matviews.ispopulated now uses.
pg_control gains an unlogged-reset LSN, shown by pg_controldata and set by pg_resetwal.
psql \d shows unlogged matviews as unlogged; pg_dump --no-unlogged-table-data does not apply to matviews.
author_claims: Unlogged matviews avoid WAL during populate and refresh, which makes refresh considerably faster; the thread gives no numbers.
Crash recovery, standby, promotion and PITR behave as expected; recovery TAP tests cover crash, standby and promotion.
An LSN-based epoch cannot falsely match a stale stamp, while a reset counter plus timeline could, as when a standby starts without standby.signal.
pg_upgrade keeps unlogged contents because pg_resetwal sets the epoch only when the reset loses data.
Two users replied +1 and listed typical rebuildable matview uses.
brief.thread_state: Jim Jones reviewed twice, fixed docs, tab completion and \d, flagged the removal of pg_class.relispopulated for client tools such as pgAdmin, and raised error message points; v6 addresses the error messages. No committer has replied, and the author still wants agreement on the approach before adding auto-refresh.
unclear: No benchmark shows the WAL or time saved on refresh.
No committer has judged whether removing relispopulated from pg_class is acceptable for client tools and extensions.
The thread does not settle how pg_dump --no-unlogged-table-data should treat unlogged matviews.
The proposal does not say how refresh materialized view concurrently works with unlogged storage.
The thread defers the auto-refresh worker and health-check function, and does not say whether they ship in core.

prior_attempts.title: Detectable crashes and unlogged table resets
prior_attempts.quote: This is too long, so let's discard this patch for now.
prior_attempts.reason: Discussion stopped after June 2021 with open questions: whether LSN or timestamp is useful (Tom Lane doubted LSN), whether to reset the counter, and whether to track promotions. The entry moved through four commitfests with no further activity, and Michael Paquier closed it because it had been idle too long.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P9 recorded the last crash recovery in pg_control so applications could detect unlogged resets, with no consumer in core. This proposal stores a similar LSN but uses it inside core to invalidate unlogged matviews, and it also covers promotion and PITR.

objections.title: pg_upgrade may mark a crash-emptied unlogged matview as populated
objections.failure_scenario: A PG20 cluster crashes and recovery resets an unlogged matview to its empty init fork, but nobody refreshes it. The user then runs pg_upgrade to PG21, and the new cluster marks the matview populated while the transferred file is empty. Queries return no rows without any error, and the user may only notice from wrong reports.
objections.argument: Patch 0002 says pg_dump reads `relpopulated <> 0` and, in binary upgrade, calls binary_upgrade_set_matview_populated(). A stale epoch stamp is non-zero, so the dump treats it as populated. The old stamp is an LSN from the old cluster's WAL, so it means nothing in the new cluster, whose epoch starts at the initdb bootstrap checkpoint. Copying the stamp would invalidate every unlogged matview on upgrade, and re-stamping would validate empty ones. The pg_upgrade claim in the brief covers only the pg_resetwal step and does not address this case.
objections.author_must_show: During pg_upgrade, what does binary_upgrade_set_matview_populated() write for an unlogged matview whose old-cluster stamp is stale, and which test covers that case?

critic.reasoning: The 0002 commit message says pg_dump reads `relpopulated <> 0`, and a stale stamp is non-zero. The 0001 text covers only the pg_resetwal step, so the material does not say what binary upgrade writes for a stale unlogged matview.

objections.title: Removing pg_class.relispopulated breaks every client for a narrow feature
objections.failure_scenario: A user upgrades to the new release and opens pgAdmin or a monitoring script that reads c.relispopulated. The query fails with "column c.relispopulated does not exist", even though the cluster has no unlogged matview. The user finds out at the first catalog query after the upgrade.
objections.argument: Message #9 shows pgAdmin failing, and message #11 notes it is not the only tool affected. The author says in message #10 that the column cannot stay because it would go stale. That is true only for unlogged matviews. A bool column could stay correct for every existing relation, with the epoch held in a separate column, so the cost would fall only on users of the new feature. The new int8 column also mixes a flag with an LSN typed as int8, and a natural rewrite such as relpopulated <> 0 reports a stale unlogged matview as populated.
objections.author_must_show: Why can't relispopulated stay as a bool that is exact for all existing relations, with the unlogged epoch kept in a separate column or in pg_matview_is_populated() only?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 explains why the bool would go stale, but only for unlogged matviews, and the thread does not discuss a separate epoch column. Catalog columns do change between major versions, so this stays fixable.

objections.title: pg_dump --no-unlogged-table-data skips unlogged tables but not unlogged matviews
objections.failure_scenario: An administrator dumps with --no-unlogged-table-data to get a fast restore without rebuildable data. Restore still runs REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW for each unlogged matview, which can take hours on large views. The administrator finds out during the restore window.
objections.argument: Message #7 says the flag ignores matviews because they "are not tables", and calls this an open question. Users read the option as "skip data I marked as disposable", and an unlogged matview is exactly that. The documentation of the option and the refresh step in the dump need one consistent rule, which the thread has not agreed.
objections.author_must_show: What should --no-unlogged-table-data do with unlogged matviews, for example dump them WITH NO DATA, and why is ignoring the flag the better contract?

critic.reasoning: Message #7 calls this an open question and nobody answered it. A dump with --no-unlogged-table-data still emits the refresh for an unlogged matview, so the restore cost is real.

objections.title: An unlogged table refreshed from a plain view already avoids WAL
objections.failure_scenario: A user who needs a WAL-free cache today can keep the query in a regular view and fill an unlogged table from it. A refresh job runs `truncate cache; insert into cache select * from cache_v` in one transaction, or builds a new unlogged table and renames it into place. To get the same result built in, every tool that reads pg_class.relispopulated must change, as pgAdmin does in message #9, and pg_control gains a new field.
objections.argument: The thread does not compare the proposal with this existing idiom, which already gives the WAL saving in message #1 and needs no catalog or pg_control change. The proposal's real gains are refresh syntax and "unpopulated, not empty" after a crash. A marker row in the same unlogged table covers the second, because crash recovery removes the marker together with the data. The thread gives no refresh numbers, so a committer would likely ask whether these conveniences justify retyping a pg_class column and changing the pg_control layout.
objections.author_must_show: What can an unlogged table filled from a regular view, with a marker row to detect a crash reset, not do that unlogged materialized views do?

critic.reasoning: The thread never compares the proposal with an unlogged table filled from a view, and gives no numbers. The marker row is weaker than the objection says, because unchecked queries read the table as empty, but that is a convenience gap.

refuted.title: Removing pg_class.relispopulated moves the cost to every catalog reader
refuted.failure_scenario: A user upgrades to the release with this patch. pgAdmin, monitoring queries and extensions that read pg_class.relispopulated or use the old rel.h macros fail with "column c.relispopulated does not exist" or no longer compile. This happens even on clusters with no unlogged matview.
refuted.argument: Message #9 shows pgAdmin breaking, and message #11 notes it is not the only such tool. Message #10 says the bool cannot stay because it could go stale, but it would go stale only for unlogged matviews, which no existing tool knows about. Keeping relispopulated for logged relations and adding a separate epoch column would leave current readers correct. The patch also widens every pg_class row from bool to int8 to serve a few matviews, and no committer has weighed the break against the gain.
refuted.author_must_show: Why not keep relispopulated unchanged for logged relations and store the unlogged epoch in a new column, so that existing tools and extensions keep working?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which makes the same point and adds the `relpopulated <> 0` hazard.

refuted.title: New pg_control invariant must be kept by every future unlogged-reset path
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a code path that discards unlogged storage, such as a new pg_resetwal mode or a recovery or restore variant, and does not advance the unlogged-reset LSN. The unlogged matview keeps a matching stamp, so queries return zero rows over the reset storage instead of raising "has not been populated". Users find out only from wrong application results.
refuted.argument: 0001 makes correctness depend on one rule: every place that resets unlogged storage must also move the LSN past any stamp. pg_resetwal already needs the special case "only when the reset actually loses data". Nothing in the design fails loudly if a future change in xlog.c, pg_resetwal or pg_upgrade misses this rule. No committer who owns recovery or pg_control has replied in the thread, so no qualified owner has accepted this liability yet.
refuted.author_must_show: What check or test would fail if a future change discarded unlogged storage without advancing the reset LSN, and which committer who owns recovery code has reviewed the invariant?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a future patch that nobody has proposed. The objection names no existing path that discards unlogged storage without the LSN update, and 0001 covers crash recovery and pg_resetwal. The missing committer reply belongs to committability.

refuted.title: Every client that reads pg_class.relispopulated breaks, for a few users' gain
refuted.failure_scenario: A user upgrades to the release with this patch and opens a materialized view in pgAdmin. pgAdmin fails with "column c.relispopulated does not exist" even though the user has no unlogged materialized views. Monitoring scripts and extensions that read the column fail the same way on their first query.
refuted.argument: Message #9 shows pgAdmin breaking, and message #11 notes that pgAdmin is not the only such tool. The cost falls on every installation, but the gain goes only to users who create unlogged materialized views. Message #10 says client tools can be patched, but that work falls on many projects outside core. The thread has no demand figures that weigh against this cost.
refuted.author_must_show: How many users need unlogged materialized views, and why does that need justify breaking every external query on pg_class.relispopulated, including on clusters that never use the feature?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The cost to clients that read relispopulated is the same point, and that objection also names a design that avoids it.

refuted.title: No numbers and no comparison with the unlogged-table workaround
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who needs a rebuildable cache today creates an unlogged table and reloads it with truncate and insert ... select in one transaction. That already avoids WAL for the data. The proposal does not show what such a user gains beyond the unpopulated state after a crash.
refuted.argument: The demand shown is the author's own motivation and two +1 replies in messages #2 and #3, which list typical uses but no WAL volumes or refresh times. The documentation says refresh becomes "considerably faster", but the thread gives no measurement. The thread never mentions the unlogged-table workaround. A committer would likely ask for numbers before accepting a pg_control change and a catalog column retype.
refuted.author_must_show: What WAL volume and refresh time does a real workload save, and which users find the unlogged-table-plus-reload workaround insufficient, and why?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1, which covers both the unlogged-table workaround and the missing refresh numbers.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 changes the pg_control layout and pg_resetwal, and patch 0002 changes the binary-upgrade path for matviews.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The epoch is set in crash recovery, and the design defines behaviour on standby, promotion and PITR.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: pg_class.relispopulated (bool) is replaced by relpopulated (int8), and pg_matview_is_populated() is added to pg_proc.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The rel.h populated macros are replaced by RelationIsPopulated() in matview.c, so extensions that use them must change.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch adds create unlogged materialized view and alter materialized view ... set { logged | unlogged }, copied from the table syntax.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump reads relpopulated <> 0, and --no-unlogged-table-data does not apply to unlogged matviews.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: psql \d reports unlogged matviews, and tab completion gains the new syntax.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new pg_control field and an epoch rule in recovery and pg_resetwal need care in later changes.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The populated check now runs through RelationIsPopulated() on matview access; relcache.c and execUtils.c are touched.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: An unlogged table filled from a regular view already avoids WAL, and the thread does not compare the two.

questions: During pg_upgrade, what does binary_upgrade_set_matview_populated() write for an unlogged matview whose old-cluster stamp is stale, and which test covers that case?
Why can relispopulated not stay as a bool that is exact for all existing relations, with the unlogged epoch kept in a separate column?
What should pg_dump --no-unlogged-table-data do with unlogged matviews, for example dump them WITH NO DATA?
How much WAL and refresh time does an unlogged matview save on a real workload, compared with an unlogged table filled from a regular view?
How does refresh materialized view concurrently work with unlogged storage?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows recovery, pg_control and pg_resetwal, and one willing to rule on the pg_class column change.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new pg_control field, the rule that every unlogged reset advances the epoch, and a changed pg_class column. All three last for every later release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted revisions up to v6 and addressed the reviewer's error message points, so the author is active in the thread.

priority.reason: Two users confirmed the use case, but the v6 series is about 83 KiB across recovery, pg_control, the catalog, pg_dump and psql. The pg_upgrade case and the catalog column shape need an answer, and a committer's view, before line-by-line review.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check what binary upgrade writes for a stale stamp, or how pg_resetwal behaves on a standby shut down in recovery. It also could not check the cost of the populated check on matview access.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add statistics refresh materialized view
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add per-view statistics for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW (execution count and last refresh time) to the statistics collector, exposed as new columns in pg_stat_all_tables and its user/sys variants. The aim was to record when and how often each materialized view was refreshed without relying on pg_stat_statements.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao objected that adding columns to pg_stat_all_tables for one utility command is a poor design: it singles out REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW over commands such as TRUNCATE or CLUSTER, would lead to many per-command columns, and the columns would be useless for most entries, which are tables. He also suggested that pg_stat_statements and log_statement could already provide the information per view. The author agreed that these tools may be sufficient for most use cases and withdrew the proposal, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's not good design to add new columns per utility command into
pg_stat_all_tables. Otherwise pg_stat_all_tables will have to have lots of
columns to expose the stats of many utility commands at last.

precedents_retrieved.title: EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE on REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, showing the plan of the view's defining SELECT (plain EXPLAIN without refreshing, EXPLAIN ANALYZE performing the refresh), analogous to existing EXPLAIN support for CREATE TABLE AS / CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW. A companion patch refactored ExecRefreshMatView into smaller functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that supporting EXPLAIN would bind REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW to having an explainable SQL plan, constraining future implementations such as incremental view maintenance, while offering little beyond explaining the view's query directly; the author agreed to withdraw the feature. The leftover refactoring patch was also not taken, because John Naylor judged it would conflict with the refactoring in the pending incremental view maintenance patch without helping it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The problem with it is that it
binds us to the assumption that REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW has an
explainable plan.

precedents_retrieved.title: Incremental Materialized View Maintenance
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add incremental materialized views (CREATE INCREMENTAL MATERIALIZED VIEW) that Postgres keeps current in the same transaction as base table changes, using AFTER triggers and transition tables. The patch computes deltas from the view definition and applies them to the view, with support for joins, some built-in aggregates, EXISTS subqueries and outer joins.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with Feedback after a month with no update. In July 2022 huyajun had reported bugs: a deadlock between TRUNCATE and concurrent INSERT, wrong counts after concurrent DELETEs, crashes on mismatched column lists, and an unwanted unique index on cross joins. The author said he was still working on them. Paquier also noted little design discussion in three years, and Greg Stark had earlier called the patch hard to review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There has been some feedback sent lately and no update
for one month, so I am marking it as RwF for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ownership error message
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW so that a permission failure reports "must be owner of materialized view" instead of the generic "must be owner of relation", by passing OBJECT_MATVIEW to the ACL check error path. The author offered to prepare back-patches for released branches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers considered the change cosmetic and argued against back-patching: the existing message is not wrong, and changing behavior in released branches can affect applications that depend on the current text. While writing a regression test, the author found that HEAD/v11 already produced the correct message because of an earlier commit. With no back-patch planned, nothing was left to fix, and the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As the plan is not to backpatch, I’ll withdraw my patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow granting of permission to REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER, and REINDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER and REINDEX grantable to non-owners, instead of being limited to the table owner, by changing the shared permission check RangeVarCallbackOwnsTable(). The preliminary patch reused the TRUNCATE privilege as a proof of concept; the intended design was a single new table privilege (e.g. REFRESH) covering all three operations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to spending one of the four free AclMode privilege bits on this, to reusing TRUNCATE, and to the backward-compatibility effect on existing owner ACLs after upgrade. The discussion then turned to how to extend the privilege-bit space (widening AclMode to 64 bits, a varlena aclitem, or a larger fixed-size aclitem) and whether to use one MAINTAIN privilege or finer-grained ones, without reaching agreement. The CommitFest manager noted no activity over two commitfests and that the thread agreed only that the problem of adding privileges extensibly had to be solved first; after no response, the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So I can't see using one of them up for
REFRESH, let alone using three of them up for REFRESH, CLUSTER and
REINDEX.

precedents_retrieved.title: Detectable crashes and unlogged table resets
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started with a per-table flag in the init fork so applications could detect that an unlogged table was reset after a crash, mainly for sharded setups where one shard can be lost. It moved to a server-wide record in pg_control of the last crash recovery (LSN, time and a counter), read through a SQL function, with an attached patch.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Discussion stopped after June 2021 with open questions: whether LSN or timestamp is useful (Tom Lane doubted LSN), whether to reset the counter, and whether to track promotions. The entry moved through four commitfests with no further activity, and Michael Paquier closed it because it had been idle too long.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This is too long, so let's discard this patch for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Unlogged relation copy is not fsync'd
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the condition in RelationCopyStorage() so that the main and other non-init forks of an unlogged relation are fsync'd after copying, for example during alter table ... set tablespace. Without the fix, a checkpoint during the copy followed by a clean shutdown and power loss can lose part of the copied file.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author found that the posted patch was still incomplete and proposed a broader backpatchable fix that calls smgrimmedsync() for all but temporary relations, with similar changes in nbtsort.c, gistbuild.c and rewriteheap.c. Noah Misch questioned part of that analysis, and no revised patch followed. After about three months with no new version, Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with feedback as waiting on the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So it seems this has been waiting for
Heikki or someone else to have time to work it for the last 3 months.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add recovery to pg_control and remove backup_label
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Andres Freund, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes backup_label and stores the recovery information in pg_control instead. pg_backup_stop() returns an updated pg_control as bytea for the backup software to store, which also avoids copying a torn pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to changing the backup API again and asked for more senior votes before a change this large. Andres Freund (his view is visible only in quoted replies) stayed on the fence, saying it helps pg_basebackup but not external backups and removes a human-readable file used for debugging. Once incremental backup was committed and depended on backup_label, Michael Paquier proposed returning the entry, and the author withdrew it rather than rework the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It would be a lot of work with all the new changes for incremental backup and since Andres and Robert appear to be very against the idea, I doubt it would be worth the effort.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert ill-considered change in pg_resetwal output.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert ill-considered change in pg_resetwal output.
Reverted commit(s): Use the terminology "WAL file" not "log file" more consistently.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 31dcfae83 changed one pg_resetwal output string, and a
corresponding test in pg_upgrade, without sufficient thought for
the consequences.  We can't change that output without creating
hazards for cross-version upgrades, since pg_upgrade needs to be able
to read the output of several different versions of pg_resetwal.
There may well be external tools with the same requirement.

For the moment, just revert those two changes.  What we really
ought to do here is have a separate, stable, easily machine-readable
output format for pg_resetwal and pg_controldata, as proposed
years ago by Alvaro.  Once that's in place and tools no longer
need to depend on the exact spelling of the human-readable output,
we can put back this change.

precedents_retrieved.summary:
Planning counters in pg_stat_statements
Threads: Planning counters in pg_stat_statements

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent was rejected for a reason that still applies here: P9 closed because it sat idle, and P3 and P14 address other ideas. Message #1 reports that earlier threads stalled because pg_class cannot be updated during recovery, and the epoch design is aimed at that blocker.

Two objections from the standards and compatibility angle. The new syntax copies CREATE UNLOGGED TABLE and SET { LOGGED | UNLOGGED }, so it follows existing practice. The extra pg_controldata line is an addition and does not change existing lines.

The LSN-epoch argument for crash, standby, promotion and PITR holds from the material. Each recovery sets an epoch above every stamp it replayed, and standbys do not read unlogged storage. One case could not be checked without the code: pg_resetwal on a standby that was shut down in recovery.

The proposal has no new privilege or exposure aspect. Creating, altering and refreshing an unlogged matview use the existing matview ownership checks. pg_matview_is_populated() reports a state that pg_matviews and pg_class already show to all users. The proposal adds no new path for running code as another role, and it does not touch RLS, authentication or resource limits.
Two objections raised. Not evaluated: hot-path cost of the new populated check, which depends on code not shown.
One objection from this angle. The auto-refresh worker and health check are deferred and could live in an extension, but they are not part of this proposal, so this review does not judge them.

Demand is plausible: the topic recurs, and the IVM and partial-refresh threads show that refresh cost hurts users. But it is not measured, and the cost of removing the pg_class column falls on everyone.
